name: Alex Lamb

papers.title: Learning Additively Compositional Latent Actions for Embodied AI
papers.abstract: Latent action models (LAMs) infer pseudo-action labels from visual transitions, providing scalable supervision from internet-scale video for embodied AI. Existing LAMs rely primarily on visual reconstruction, which pushes the latent to encode any cue predictive of the next frame, including background appearance and future shortcuts. The resulting latents entangle motion with nuisance content and their norms decouple from motion magnitude, weakening cross-environment transfer and providing poor supervision for downstream policies. We argue that these failures stem from the absence of structural priors on the latent space, and propose to endow the latent space with an explicit algebraic structure. We introduce the Additively Compositional Latent Action Model (AC-LAM), which imposes a structural constraint on the latent action space, requiring latent actions to compose additively over time. Such additivity is naturally satisfied by rigid-body motion, yet violated by many nuisance signals. We show theoretically that this single constraint induces identity, inverse, and cycle-consistency structure in the latent space, and discourages additively-separable nuisance components such as scene-constant and goal-only offsets. Empirically, we develop a diagnostic suite that probes these algebraic properties and shows that AC-LAM learns more physically meaningful, displacement-calibrated latents with markedly less scene-identity leakage than prior LAMs. The same latents translate into consistent gains on downstream policy learning across both simulated and real-robot tabletop manipulation under in- and out-of-distribution conditions.
